intended_object: The canonical natural transformation τ_{<b} ∘ τ_{≥a} ∘ τ_{<b} ⟶ τ_{<b} ∘ τ_{≥a} for a t-structure, induced by the counit τ_{<b} → id (from the docstring). In the file it is an intermediate step towards the commutation isomorphism τ_{<b}τ_{≥a} ≅ τ_{≥a}τ_{<b}.
explanation: The body whiskers the counit `t.eTruncLTι b : τ_{<b} ⟶ 𝟭` on the left by `τ_{<b} ⋙ τ_{≥a}`, then applies the associator and the right unitor. That gives exactly the map the docstring describes, so the construction is correct. It is only used in this file, where `IsIso` is proved for it (line 477) and it is combined with `eTruncLTGELTSelfToLTGE` (line 502) to build the isomorphism that says the two truncations commute. So it is a helper morphism in the proof of that commutation, not a notion with its own definition in the literature. Even read as a mathematical object, it would be faithful: there is nothing wrong with it and nothing to generalize.
